title: Assessment of Epithelial Barrier Integrity by TEER and FITC-Dextran Permeability Assays
markdown:
## Protocol: Assessment of Caco-2 epithelial barrier integrity in Transwell monolayers using TEER and FITC-dextran permeability

### Overview

This protocol outlines the procedures for assessing Caco-2 epithelial barrier integrity in Transwell monolayers. It covers cell seeding and differentiation, maintenance of electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (TEER) equipment, TEER measurement techniques, and FITC-dextran permeability assays. The process spans from initial coating and seeding on Day 0 through a culture period of up to 3 weeks, with regular medium changes and periodic integrity assessments.

### Materials/Reagents

- Rat tail collagen coating solution
- Sterile PBS
- Complete cell culture medium
- 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA
- Trypan Blue
- 1% Tergazyme
- Sterile distilled water (dH2O)
- 70% Ethanol
- 4 kDa FITC-dextran
- Pre-warmed growth media

### Equipment

- Transwell inserts (collagen-coated)
- Cell culture flasks
- 15 mL Falcon tubes
- Microcentrifuge tubes
- EVOM3 meter
- STX2 electrode
- Vacuum line with 200 μL pipette tips
- Humidified incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2)
- Biosafety cabinet
- Microplate reader (fluorescence)

### Safety & Sterility

- Maintain sterile conditions throughout all steps involving cell handling and reagent preparation.
- Use a vacuum line fitted with a 200 μL pipette tip when aspirating from apical chambers to prevent membrane damage.
- Avoid touching the membrane with pipette tips or electrodes during aspiration and measurement.
- Handle the STX2 electrode carefully: never immerse the head, cable, or connector; only soak the metal tips.
- Store FITC-dextran stock solutions protected from light.
- Perform cleaning and disinfection of electrodes using ethanol and sterile water as specified to prevent cross-contamination.

## Transwell Seeding and Monolayer Differentiation

### Day 0: Transwell Coating

1. Add 100 μL of rat tail collagen coating solution to the apical chamber (inside the insert). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Ensure the apical surface has enough liquid to prevent the membrane from drying out; an even coating is critical for uniform cell confluence. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S02 -->
2. Incubate the plate for either 2 h at 37 °C for same-day use or overnight at 4 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S03 -->
3. Immediately before seeding, aspirate the coating solution from both chambers and wash twice with sterile PBS, using 300 μL for the apical side and 800 μL for the basolateral side. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S04 -->
4. Remove PBS after the final wash. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S05 -->
> **Operational constraint:** When aspirating from the apical chamber, use a vacuum line fitted with a 200 μL pipette tip and avoid touching the membrane to prevent damage. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S06 -->

### Day 0: Cell Harvesting and Counting

1. Aspirate the medium from a confluent flask of cells and wash the monolayer once with 8-10 mL of sterile PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S01 -->
2. Remove the PBS, add 2 mL of 0.25% trypsin-EDTA to the flask, and incubate at 37 °C for 10-25 min or until cells have detached. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Do not shake or tap the flask during the trypsinization process, as this can cause cell clumping and lead to inaccurate cell counting. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S03 -->
3. Neutralize the trypsin by adding 4 mL of complete medium. Gently pipette up and down to create a single-cell suspension. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S04 -->
4. Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL Falcon tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S05 -->
5. To determine cell viability and concentration, mix 50 μL of the cell suspension with 50 μL of Trypan Blue. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S06 -->

### Day 0: Seeding Transwells

1. Using the cell count from the previous step, calculate the volume needed to achieve a final density of 1.0-1.5 × 10^5 cells per insert. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S01 -->
2. Resuspend the required cell pellet in enough complete medium to deliver this density in 200 μL per insert. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S02 -->
3. Add 600 μL of fresh medium to the basolateral chamber of each well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S03 -->
4. Add 200 μL of the prepared cell suspension to the apical chamber of each insert. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S04 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Pipette the cell suspension gently into the center of the insert to ensure an even monolayer. Avoid touching the membrane with the pipette tip. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S05 -->

### Day 0: Initial Incubation

1. Place the plate in a humidified incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T3-S01 -->

### every 2 days starting day one post-seeding

1. Change the medium in both apical and basolateral chambers every 2 days starting day one post-seeding. Aspirate the old media, add 600 μL of fresh medium to the basolateral chamber of each well, and then add 200 μL of fresh medium to the apical chamber of each well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T5-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** When aspirating from the apical chamber, use a vacuum line fitted with a 200 μL pipette tip and avoid touching the membrane to prevent damage. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T5-S02 -->

### Days 1-21: Culture Period

1. Culture the cells for 1-3 weeks (or according to experimental timeline). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T6-S01 -->

## Electrode Maintenance and TEER Measurement

### Weekly: Electrode Deep Cleaning

1. Take a new, sterile 24-well plate and prepare a cleaning station by adding 1.5 mL of 1% Tergazyme to one well and 1.5 mL of sterile dH2O to an adjacent well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S01 -->
2. Carefully place only the metal tips of the STX2 electrode into the well containing 1% Tergazyme. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S02 -->
3. Set a timer and allow the tips to soak for 15 min. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S03 -->
4. After the soak, move the electrode tips into the well containing sterile dH2O. Rinse the tips thoroughly by dipping them up and down five times. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S04 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Handle the STX2 electrode carefully to ensure accurate readings and long-term use: never immerse the electrode head, cable, or connector (only the tips), always lift the electrode by its body, and do not soak it in alcohol for more than 30 min to avoid damaging the protective coating. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S05 -->
5. Lift the electrode out of the water and let it air-dry completely inside a biosafety cabinet before starting the measurement or storing it in its original box. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S06 -->

### each day before taking TEER measurements

1. Take a new, sterile 24-well plate. Add 1.5 mL of each of the following solutions to separate wells: 70% ethanol (for disinfection), sterile dH2O (for rinsing), sterile PBS (for equilibration). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S01 -->
2. Connect the EVOM3 to the STX2 electrode cable and turn on the EVOM3. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S02 -->
3. Place only the metal tips of the electrode into the well with 70% ethanol and let them soak for 10 min. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S03 -->
4. After 10 min, move the electrode tips into the well with sterile dH2O. Rinse the tips thoroughly by dipping them up and down five times. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S04 -->
5. Move the rinsed tips into the well with sterile PBS. Allow the electrode to equilibrate for at least 5 min. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S05 -->

### After 5 min of equilibration in PBS

1. Check the reading on the EVOM3 meter. It should display a low resistance value (e.g., 0-40 Ω). If the reading is inaccurate, calibrate and re-equilibrate the electrode according to the manufacturer's protocol before proceeding with measurements. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T2-S01 -->

### TEER Measurement Day

1. Proceed with the TEER measurement and perform the final cleanup procedure after all measurements. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S01 -->
2. Remove the cell culture plate from the incubator and allow it to equilibrate to room temperature for 15-20 min inside a biosafety cabinet. This is critical for obtaining stable and reproducible resistance readings. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Do not change the cell medium before TEER measurement, as this may cause inconsistent day-to-day readings. If a medium change is required, perform it only after completing the TEER measurement. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S03 -->
> **Operational constraint:** For immediate TEER measurements performed after experimental stimulation (e.g., infection or treatment), always include an untreated control group for proper comparison of TEER values. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S04 -->
3. Prepare the EVOM3 and STX2 electrode for measurement as described in the daily preparation steps. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S05 -->
4. To measure a sample well, carefully position the electrode so that the shorter tip is inside the apical chamber, and the longer tip is in the basolateral chamber. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S06 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Ensure the electrode is positioned consistently in the same location for every well and is not touching the cell monolayer or the bottom of the plate. The tips must be fully submerged in the medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S07 -->
5. Wait for the resistance reading on the EVOM3 display to stabilize, then record the value in ohms (Ω). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S08 -->
6. To move between wells while maintaining sterility and preventing cross-contamination (especially when working with different treatments or infectious agents), follow this cleaning procedure: [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S09 -->
7. Briefly dip the electrode tips into a well containing 70% ethanol for 2 min. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S10 -->
8. Immediately rinse the tips by dipping them into a separate well containing sterile PBS to remove residual ethanol before proceeding to the next sample. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S11 -->
9. After all measurements are complete, perform the final cleaning procedure. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S12 -->
10. Plot TEER values (Ω) on the y-axis and days post-seeding on the x-axis for data visualization. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S13 -->

### Post-Measurement Cleanup

1. Soak the electrode tips in 70% ethanol for 10 min. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T4-S01 -->
2. Rinse the tips thoroughly with sterile distilled water by dipping them up and down five times. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T4-S02 -->
3. Let the electrode air-dry completely inside a biosafety cabinet. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T4-S03 -->
4. Once completely dry, store the electrode in its original box, protected from light, to prepare it for the next use. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T4-S04 -->

## FITC-dextran Permeability Assay

### Assay Preparation

1. Prepare a 10 mg/mL stock solution of 4 kDa FITC-dextran in sterile dH2O. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Prepare the stock solution in microcentrifuge tubes, wrap them in aluminum foil, and store them at 4 °C, protected from light. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S02 -->
2. Prepare a 2 mg/mL working solution of FITC-dextran by diluting a 10 mg/mL stock solution 1:5 in prewarmed growth media. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S03 -->
3. Prepare the following controls for your experiment: [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S04 -->
4. Negative control (intact barrier): Use untreated, healthy cell monolayers to define basal permeability. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S05 -->
5. Positive control (maximum permeability): Use a cell-free, collagen-coated Transwell insert to define maximum diffusion. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S06 -->

### Assay Execution

1. Gently aspirate the medium from both apical and basolateral chambers. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T1-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** When aspirating from the apical chamber, use a vacuum line fitted with a 200 μL pipette tip and avoid touching the membrane to prevent damage. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T1-S02 -->
2. Wash the monolayers three times by adding 300 μL (apical) and 800 μL (basolateral) of sterile PBS for each wash. Aspirate PBS between washes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T1-S03 -->
3. After the final wash, aspirate the PBS from both apical and basolateral chambers. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T1-S04 -->
4. Add 600 μL of fresh medium to the basolateral chamber of each well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T1-S05 -->
5. Add 200 μL of the 2 mg/mL FITC-dextran working solution to the apical chamber of each well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T1-S06 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Ensure that no FITC-dextran contaminates the basolateral medium, as this would falsely reflect permeability readings. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T1-S07 -->
6. Incubate the plate in a humidified incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2) in the dark for 3 h. Note: The incubation time may require optimization depending on the experimental model. Time-course sampling (e.g., every 30 min) can be performed to determine the linear transport phase of FITC-dextran permeability. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T1-S08 -->
7. After incubation, carefully remove the apical chamber and collect the medium from the basolateral chamber of each well (~600 μL) in microcentrifuge tubes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T1-S09 -->

### Fluorescence Measurement

1. Transfer 100 μL from each collected sample into a clear-bottom 96-well plate. Plate each sample as a technical triplicate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T2-S01 -->
2. Prepare a standard curve in the same plate by performing 1:2 serial dilutions of the 2 mg/mL FITC-dextran working solution as triplicates. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T2-S02 -->
3. Add 100 μL of cell-free medium to three empty wells to serve as the blank (for background subtraction). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T2-S03 -->
4. Read the fluorescence on a microplate reader at an excitation wavelength of ~490 nm and an emission wavelength of ~520 nm. Record the relative fluorescence units (RFU) for all wells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T2-S04 -->

### Data Analysis

1. Calculate basolateral FITC-dextran concentration: a. Calculate the average RFU of the blank wells. Subtract this value from all standard and sample RFU values to correct for background fluorescence. b. Plot the background-subtracted RFU values of the standards on the y-axis against their known concentrations (in μg/mL) on the x-axis. c. Perform a linear regression analysis to generate the equation of the line (y = mx + b) and its coefficient of determination (R2). Note: A valid standard curve ideally should have an R2 value > 0.95. d. Use the linear regression formula to calculate the concentration of FITC-dextran in each experimental sample using the following equation. x = (y−b)/m x = basal FITC-dextran concentration (μg/mL) y = background-subtracted RFU of your sample. m = slope of the standard curve line. b = y-intercept of the standard curve line. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T3-S01 -->
2. Average the calculated concentrations from your technical triplicates to obtain the final permeability value (in μg/mL) for each biological replicate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T3-S02 -->
3. Plot permeability values (μg/mL) on the y-axis and days post-seeding on the x-axis for data visualization. Note: Although FD4 permeability is presented as concentration (μg/mL) in this protocol, users may calculate apparent permeability (Papp, cm/s) using standard equations if transport kinetics analysis is required. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T3-S03 -->
